summary: Model pin misattributed to wrong tenant after edge auth token rotation causing mixed-model responses
description: Issue summary: Several NovaChat tenants reported interleaved responses where some requests returned outputs from redwood-chat-v2.1.0 while other requests in the same session returned redwood-chat-v1.9.8. This appeared during a routine edge authentication token rotation window.
description_impact: Impact: Customer-facing chats sporadically returned older-model outputs (~5-7% of requests) for affected tenants. Customer observed evidence of degraded answer consistency and minor regression in hallucination rate. A dedicated customer (NovaChat) with strict SLAs is impacted; potential business risk if not remediated.
description_environment: Environment: Production (prod), region us-east-1, NovaChat dedicated cluster behind edge-proxy pool EP-22. Traffic primarily routed through canary edge nodes during the rotation window.
description_steps_to_reproduce: Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger an auth token rotation on the edge-proxy (simulate by swapping signing key and forcing reissue). 2) Send a mix of long and short chat requests with the same tenant session cookie. 3) Observe model assignment headers (X-Model-Pin, X-Tenant-ID) and resulting responses. 4) Reproduce by enabling extended logging on edge and routing services; curl sample included in investigation notes.
observed_behavior: Observed: During the rotation, a subset of requests had their X-Tenant-ID header rewritten to the edge canonical ID (edge-ephemeral) instead of the original tenant ID during the token refresh handshake. The routing layer persisted the model pin using the canonical ID, effectively binding the pin to the wrong tenant namespace. Subsequent requests from the real tenant were routed to the fall-back model variant.
expected_behavior: Expected: Token rotation should preserve original tenant identifier and session affinity headers. Model pin information must be stored against the tenant namespace in the routing cache so tenant-specific pins are never associated with edge-internal identities.
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced locally with a token reissue script and curl: when Authorization re-negotiation occurred mid-request, the edge inserted 'x-tenant-id: edge-ephemeral' into the forwarded request in ~6/1000 attempts.
- Trace 2026-03-13-09:03:21 (trace id t-7f3d) shows header canonicalization hook ran after auth refresh.
- Cache keys in routing-cache (rc-neo) show entries like 'tenant:edge-ephemeral:route-pin' created at 09:03:22.
- Hypothesis: edge-auth middleware's atomic swap briefly emits a synthetic tenant identifier for internal bookkeeping; an ordering bug lets the routing middleware run while the synthetic id is present.
- Additional note: affected requests correlate with canary nodes EP-22/EP-23 which shipped edge-proxy change PR 1987 last week.
- Reproduced on staging with controlled rotation; root cause narrowed to edge-proxy auth pipeline order-of-operations.
- No evidence of DB corruption; this is a transient cache misattribution issue, not persisted tenant metadata mutation.
comments: [2026-03-13 09:12] Priya Menon (Support): Customer reported mixed-model outputs after our scheduled edge token rotation at 09:00. They provided sample session IDs and two request traces. Asked for immediate triage and whether we can pause further rotations.

[2026-03-13 09:27] Diego Alvarez (SRE): Got initial traces. Suspect header rewrite during auth refresh. Spun up a reproducer against staging; able to see tenant header replaced in a small fraction of requests. Assigning to edge team for urgent fix.

[2026-03-13 10:05] Marisol Cheng (Edge Eng): Confirmed ordering bug in middleware pipeline introduced in PR 1987. Adding hotfix candidate to edge-proxy (PR 1999). Planning to deploy to canary nodes EP-22/EP-23 only and monitor for absence of misattribution.

[2026-03-13 13:40] Priya Menon (Support): Communicated to NovaChat that we identified a likely cause and are deploying a targeted hotfix to canary edge nodes. Customer asked for a workaround to reconcile pins on affected sessions.

[2026-03-14 02:15] Diego Alvarez (SRE): Deployed PR 1999 to EP-22/EP-23 canaries. Observed zero occurrences in 4h of simulated rotations. Running pin-reconciliation script for affected tenant cookies to rebind pins to correct tenant namespace. Notifying customer of mitigation steps.
workaround: Workaround applied: 1) Deployed hotfix to canary edge nodes to stop emitting synthetic tenant IDs during auth swap. 2) Ran a tenant pin reconciliation job that scans routing-cache for 'edge-ephemeral' keys and re-associates model-pin entries back to original tenant IDs for NovaChat sessions. 3) Advised NovaChat to pause client token re-issuance during active heavy sessions until fix is fully rolled out to all edges.
resolution: Mitigation: Hotfix PR 1999 merged; rollout scheduled to full edge pool after additional monitoring window. Reconciliation script completed for NovaChat (approx 8k affected cache entries). Follow-up: add unit/integration tests to edge-auth pipeline to assert tenant-id preservation and add metric 'edge.auth.synthetic-tenant-emitted' to alert on any regression. Postmortem and release notes to follow in Confluence.
next_steps: 1) Roll out hotfix to remaining edge nodes in controlled waves. 2) Harden middleware ordering by moving routing decision after auth finalization. 3) Add synthetic-tenant emission alert and a runbook step to immediately run pin-reconciliation if detected. 4) Postmortem and share with customer.
